facts.status_note: Sources list it as abandoned; no source we read describes the site now.

corrections.why: Both firelookout.com and the Oregon Lookouts index describe this crow's nest as abandoned, and the index uses the word Gone only for Damewood Point. No source we read says the structure was removed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A 1911 Eugene Guard report, quoted on Forest Lookouts, shows a Deer Butte lookout in use in August 1911. firelookout.com dates its crow's nest to the 1920s. The story reports both dates and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: Do not confuse this with the Deer Butte in Klamath County on the Deschutes National Forest. That site had a 40-foot tower built in 1934 and was gone by 1965 (willhiteweb.com/oregon_lookouts/deer_butte/tower_010.htm). It came up in both searches and was not used. Two WebSearch calls found no Lane County history beyond the three pages above. The brief lists kind platform, but firelookout.org says Crowsnest and no source says whether the crow's nest sat on a tree or a platform, so kind was left alone. A TopoQuest summit listing (5301 ft) appeared in search only and was not read, so it is not used. The brief's status gone is not supported by any source for this site; see corrections. Verification 2026-10-10: the word 'summit' and the phrase 'photos taken there' were removed because no source says either; the 5,298-foot figure is the lookout's elevation on firelookout.com, and evidence quotes were added for the elevation, the Santiam fire, the sighting location and the 1915, 1918 and 1933 items.
